title: 【CLO5.2】Let's learn 3D clothing together~ The CLO5.2 new features live broadcast replay is here!!!
description: Wasn't the recording uploaded really quickly this time? Hurry up and watch to learn~ If you think the upload speed this time was fast, give Xiao C a "speed" in the chat~~~
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am Samantha from Cloud Shanghai.  
Today, I will give you a live broadcast of the new 5.2 features.  
After you install the software, you will find that many of our tools seem to be gone.  
But in fact, they are not gone; rather, they have been integrated into tool groups after version 5.2.  
For example, our Edit Pattern tool.  
If you press and hold, you will see that all tools related to point and line editing are integrated into it.  
If you want to revert to the old tool layout mode,  
go to User Settings,  
then to the User Interface.  
You will find a Tool Group option.  
After turning off this button, you can return to the old version of the tool layout mode.  

Now, I want to talk about our project file storage.  
This is an update related to the tool layout.  
When you click File and then Save Project,  
it will save both the project file and the tool layout.  
Previously, the tool layout only supported a single view.  
Now, we can save a tool layout with four views.  
To enable this, go to Settings,  
then User Settings,  
and under Default File,  
there is a shortcut option to save four angles.  
After selecting this option, you can save shortcuts to save four views.  

Next, let's move on to our sticker classification tool.  
First, select the sticker on your background.  
Then, open the Attribute Editor.  
You will see a Classification box.  
Click it, and you will find three types of sticker classifications.  
Choose Logo Classification here.  
You can also create a custom classification.  
For example, delete the existing one,  
and enter "Four-Wings Print" in the classification list.  

Next, I want to talk about an update to our Quick Photo function.  
Go to the Quick Photo 3D window.  
Let's save a quick photo first.  
You can save a single quick photo or multiple.  
Here, you can set a view or a custom view.  
On the left, set the picture size.  
On the right, set the number of displays.  
The maximum number now can reach 10.  
There is also an option to save HTML files.  
After enabling it, your quick photo will be saved as an HTML file.  
When you open this HTML file,  
you can click Next to switch to the next quick photo.  

Now, I will talk about an update to our video feature.  
Other options remain unchanged.  
There is just one more option below Duration, which is Save HTML File.  
After saving, the duration will be grayed out because the saved HTML file is a fixed rotation picture.  
It can be used to create GIFs or web-based rotation videos.  
Click the Record button to start recording.  
After recording, click Save to save the file.  
Here, I'll show you a saved HTML file.  
After saving, you can save an AVI file as well.  
You can save both AVI and HTML files.  
Click Next to see the next picture.  

Next, I want to talk about a newly released mode: the Material List Mode.  
Go to the upper right corner of the model window and click it.  
You can switch to Material List Mode at the bottom.  
After switching, a BOM (Bill of Materials) editor page will open.  
Here, you can see the fabric size, material volume, and price.  
The material volume used for this fabric is determined by the placement of the sheet in the flower arrangement.  
Go to the Flower Arrangement Mode.  
Click the upper right corner of the window to open the BOM editor.  
You can also open the BOM editor in other modes.  
When you do an initial arrangement, click Update in the BOM editor,  
and you will see the material volume change accordingly.  
Click the Settings button on the currency unit to switch the currency.  
For example, change it to RMB (CNY).  
Find CNY and close the button; the currency unit will be updated to RMB CNY.  

You can also choose different colors and edit them.  
The system will show the cost of the current color and the total cost of all colors.  
Prices below can also be changed, as well as the unit length.  
Units can be changed to inches, centimeters, millimeters, etc.  
Next to it, the cost is displayed, and below is the total price.  
This content will appear in our Closet Process List.  

Next, I want to talk about some AVT files we use for our virtual models.  
You can see rectangular objects in this window, which are the original objects.  
To open these files, just open the AVT folder.  
Inside, there is a 3D Shape folder containing AVT files for these envelopes.  
Next, we will make an arrangement for it.  
Open the Virtual Model Editor, go to the Arrangement page, and add an arrangement board.  
Adjust the size of the arrangement board to fit the AVT file of the envelope.  
Adjust the position of the arrangement board accordingly.  
After installation, turn off the editor and open the arrangement point.  
You can arrange the board to this AVT file as usual in clothing production.  

To adapt to more envelopes, the AVT file can be transformed.  
Select the AVT file, go to the main folder, and find the arrangement board.  
You will see specifications showing the XYZ size.  
Uncheck Fixed Proportion, then modify sizes individually.  
You can also click the icon in the upper right corner of the arrangement board  
to switch to Transform Arrangement Board mode to transform or modify the AVT file or envelope.  
After transformation, switch back to the ordinary arrangement board.  
You may find parts move to the bottom of the grid.  
Select and move the virtual model to the ground to align the AVT file with the grid bottom.  

Next, I want to talk about an update to our copper model.  
First, let's look at the copper model.  
We have added models for children aged 6 to 18 months.  
Double-click to open the child model in the window.  
Navigate to the Size File folder, open the corresponding model folder, and double-click to open.  
There are copper model sizes for different months.  
You can apply directly or edit virtually in the virtual model editor.  
Our model can also have shoe changes.  
Find the corresponding shoe file folder and open it.  
You can apply it similarly for other models.  

Next, an update on our aluminum model.  
Previously, posture was divided into wearing high heels and flat shoes.  
Now, this distinction is removed.  
Just open the model and choose whether to keep the current shoe posture.  
If unchecked, the foot will become flat shoe posture.  
Toggle the option to switch between normal high heel and flat shoe posture.  
If you switch shoes, the posture automatically updates without manual adjustment.  

Now, let's talk about the V2 model.  
You can also play animations.  
Open a costume, go to Animation Mode, then open the V2 folder, then the Motion folder.  
Select motion; the first two options are default.  
Click OK.  
You can move the perspective and adjust playback speed to view the model's actions.  
Click Record to start recording the show.  
Because recording takes time, I will stop recording now.  
Then reset the position and switch modes.  

Next, I will explain updates to the 3D window.  
The biggest update in 5.2 is the addition of real-time rendering in the 3D window.  
Open a costume, and in the upper left corner of the 3D window, there is a High-Quality Rendering button.  
Click it to render the costume with textures.  
Fabric texture will look more realistic.  
You can open high-quality rendering after quick photo to get better-quality quick photos.  
Comparing three images: left is normal quick photo, middle is quick photo after high-quality rendering, right is rendering function output.  
Real-time rendering effects are obviously better than normal pictures, though still some difference remains.  
For high-quality images, using rendering is recommended.  

Previously, some lace fabrics had transparent effects where two layers overlapped strangely.  
After enabling high-quality rendering, this problem is solved.  
You can clearly see the lace fabric layering.  

Next is an update to the Quick Simulation Mode.  
After opening simulation mode, you will see three speeds: fast, normal, and the completed simulation animation.  
Simulation is now complete and moved to Show Mode.  
You can see the difference between the old and new simulation model names on our official website.  
Left is old, right is new, with corresponding function introductions.  

Next, the default physical property variables have been updated.  
Curve intensity and other data are now softer.  

Now, some new features in the 2D window.  
First, an update to parallel open edit.  
Open a costume, select the edit tool.  
In the 2D window, on the right in front of the line, you can see section editing.  
You can adjust and open parallel editing of pattern sections, then simulate.  
Lines connect at points; you can right-click to link or unlink points.  

Next, symmetrical version DXF is supported.  
You can set the version as symmetrical open and editing by selecting the Outline tool, cutting along the middle line, deleting half, then right-clicking to enable symmetrical editing.  
You can cut and sew while opening the pattern, combining parts together.  

Next, basic line creation and editing functions.  
Previously, basic lines could not be edited or created directly.  
After 5.2, you can edit and create basic lines.  
On the left side of the 2D window, a new Lock button is added.  
Use the Edit Pattern tool to select basic lines for editing.  
Right-click to select segments, move, carve, or change length (e.g., set length to 300mm).  
You can create guidelines and intuition lines (canvass).  

Next, difference between basic lines and inner lines:  
Inner lines influence the 3D shape of the costume and add details like fold lines or face lines.  
Basic lines act as markers, e.g., chest line, waistline, hip line.  
Draw lines on the front pattern; internal lines affect the grid count, basic lines do not.  
Colors differentiate lines: red for inner lines, blue for basic lines.  
Use basic lines first for faster processing, then internal lines.  

Drawing base lines:  
Single machine start and double machine end.  
Hold Control and left-click to input points for base lines; release Control to draw straight lines.  
G-shaped base line tool allows dragging or inputting specific values.  
Multidirectional base line tool can draw lines of specific length.  
Circular base lines can also be drawn.  
Lines are locked by default; unlock to edit, move, stretch, rotate.  
Categorize lines as parts or plates for pocket creation.  

Next, update on line addition function.  
Open a new costume.  
Use the edit board tool, right-click to add line with specific value.  
This creates a lock style.  
For example, a skirt’s hip can be tightened or loosened with extension boards.  
Add line sets direction, width, and length.  
Simulate to see the effect of loosening the waist for a harmonious fit.  

Next, extension functions:  
Choose shoe length, right-click to rotate line, set direction, transfer line, confirm length.  
Embroidery can be transferred to chest area.  

Next, a new tool: Extend Line.  
In the 2D window, long press the extension board tool.  
Set first and second section length lines, basic lines, and extension directions.  
Set extension length and direction (start, end, or both).  
Extend basic line section to 150mm, confirm extension.  
Simulate changes in cross-section amount.  
Adjust lower plate on side as needed.  
Merge boards if interlacing amount is insufficient.  

Update on extension board point function:  
Previously, extension was only on one side.  
Now, clicking the middle extension line allows extension on both ends simultaneously.  
Simulate to see increased interlacing.  

Next, extension function:  
In 2D window, select extension tool.  
Set extension line and type.  
Set number of extensions (e.g., four), width at start and end, proportion adjustments.  
Preview board shape changes.  
Create cutouts at the end with options for opening or both ends.  
Boards can be auto-sealed without manual sealing.  
Simulate to see cutout effects, which correspond to 3D circular effects.  

Next, board lock function:  
On the left of 2D window, there is a lock menu.  
You can lock board outside line, inside line, basic line, etc.  
Locking prevents selection and editing.  
Right-click to unlock all boards or specific lines.  
Locking can be applied to single lines or points (e.g., embroidery points).  

Next, rotation logo function update:  
Select the edit focus tool to rotate logos horizontally to numeric states.  

Next, board group function:  
Useful for editing multilayer garments like down jackets or layered dresses.  
In 2D window, select the front pattern piece, set as a group.  
Select layered boards, set groups, and embroidered boards similarly.  
Selecting one board can select the entire group for pressure adjustments.  
You can select single boards by clicking again.  

Next, function update for changing board length:  
In 2D window, select sleeve and front boards for length comparison.  
Right-click to move the board to the intersection point, facilitating continuous line drawing between boards.  
Adjust order of boards to control overlap.  
Use basic line tool to draw separation lines.  
Right-click sleeve to rotate it (around X axis).  
Cut colloidal contours into seams for simulation.  
Separation lines are visible in 3D window.  

Next, sewing line update:  
Select sewing line, open attribute editor, find 3D sewing line option.  
Open to see different sewing line effects.  
Change hairline sticker to switch between hooking-in and bulge seam effects.  

Next, sticker code tool:  
Select edge of sticker, open code tool in attribute editor, input specific numbers as codes.  
You can use shortcut keys to enter codes quickly.  
Different numbers display below the sticker for identification.  

Next, color search function:  
Select fabric (e.g., jacket), open color library on the right.  
Use search bar to enter color name, press Enter to find and apply the color.  

Next, change in sticker type:  
Select edge sticker, apply a whole sticker.  
Preview content will change; pull frame to see different sticker types.  
Different sticker types affect physical properties (e.g., hardness).  
Simulate to see changes between harder and softer stickers.  

Next, update to 3D zipper:  
Previously, 3D zippers could only be created in the 3D window.  
Now, they can be created in 2D window with the same operation method.  
Click to create, simulate to see zipper automatically pull up.  
Turn off simulation to pull zipper down, then simulate again to see it open.  
Upper zipper is new content.  
In 3D editor, you can pull zippers and modify upper and lower zipper samples, changing zipper types.  
Zipper materials can be modified independently;  
For example, zipper pull as metal, zipper tape as plastic, with separate color settings.  

Next, chain function:  
Like the zipper, chains can be created in the 2D window.  
Create by single start and double end points.  
Chain will be created accordingly.  

Next, side creation:  
Side is a new addition in 2D window.  
Create by single start and original point, click again to complete side creation.  
Simulate to see side sewn to skirt bottom.  

Next, update to chain function:  
We have two types of sewing line names: default and OBJ name.  
Previously, only line name and free name existed; now OBJ name line is added.  
You can add OBJ name lines to sewing lines for clearer identification.  

Next, update to sewing line background:  
In sewing window, click sewing line.  
Now background can be a picture instead of pure background.  
You can change the picture and color overlay on the background.  
A ground shadow option adds shadows under the model for more realism.  
Transparency settings can be toggled without losing shadow effect.  
You can design custom text or image backgrounds.  
Images will stretch to fit; you can adjust size to avoid distortion.  

Next, hair transformation after 5.2:  
Open transparency settings.  
Hair color can be changed (e.g., to red).  
Use the color picker to apply a rainbow transformation.  
Adjust color range and middle position for gradient effects.  
Lighting function can be applied to hair for radiance.  

Next, lighting updates:  
After installing 5.2, you will find more lighting options.  
Default light is the original light in the light attribute.  
Rendering can randomly perform light rendering with environment maps.  
Environment maps support HDR files that affect lighting effects.  

Original light is a single light on the far right, which can be toggled to skylight.  
Below are options to add lights.  
G-shaped light:  
Generated at dot coordinates, position adjustable in 3D window.  
Curve shows reflection direction.  
Intensity can be adjusted (e.g., set to 10) to highlight effects.  
The light casts direct illumination with shadows behind.  
Sphere lamp:  
Scattered light without specific direction, softer and weaker than G-shaped light.  
Used to fill lighting gently.  

Spotlight:  
Adjust angle to set lighting direction.  
Adjust intensity and smoothing for soft light edges.  
Hand-held editor allows adjusting minimum and maximum angles of the spotlight cone.  
Larger angles mean wider and softer light spread.  
Shadow radius controls softness and size of shadows on the ground.  

Purple light:  
Parallel uniform light simulating sunlight effects.  
Color can be adjusted (e.g., light yellow for dusk or sunset effects).  

IES light:  
Uses real light data files (IES files) for accurate lighting.  
You can import your own IES files.  
Adjust position and intensity for customized lighting effects.  

That’s all for today’s 5.2 new feature live broadcast.  
Thank you all for watching.  
If you have any questions, please send them via chat.  
I will reply, and answers will appear in the comments.  

Q&A highlights:  
- Can the chain be separated from the belt and tongue? Currently, no; separation requires scanning the actual chain.  
- Will 3D and real clothes look alike? If using real fabric and correct sewing techniques, the similarity is about 91%.  
- Can zippers be printed with logos? This depends on real fabric use; it is a 3D design feature, not 4D.  
- Can seam lines (铭线) be imported into other 3D software? Yes, as long as you export the entire garment as an OBJ file, it can be imported and read by other 3D software.  
- Where to download recorded videos? Please follow our official WeChat account, where recordings will be posted.  
- How to make invisible and waterproof zippers? Invisible zippers can be normally sewn with the zipper pull as an OBJ attachment since the zipper is not visible when closed. For open zipper display, create small panels with zipper tape textures.  
- Can models be shared? Models cannot be shared due to licensing.  
- How to remove underwear textures on models? Select the model body, go to the Attribute Editor, and replace with textures without underwear.  
- How to export 3D software files? Export as OBJ or FBX files supported by other 3D software.  
- How to add models to rendering background? In the rendering window, select background options or import your own images for application.  
- How to adjust flower size in flower arrangement? Use a 1:1 size flower draft for best effect; adjust in software if necessary.  
- Can IES lighting files be imported? Yes, the system includes nine IES files, and you can also import your own.  

If you have no more questions, today’s live broadcast ends here.  
Please also pay attention to our basic course live broadcast tomorrow at 8 p.m.  
Thank you all for your support today.  
Thank you.

chunks.content: # CLO5.2 New Features Overview This document details the new features and updates introduced in CLO version 5.2, focusing on tool layout integration, project file storage, sticker classification, photo and video functions, material management, virtual models, 3D and 2D window enhancements, lighting, and Q&A clarifications. It is optimized for semantic search and embedding with clear technical explanations, procedures, and examples. --- ## Tool Layout Integration and User Interface Settings This section covers the integration of tools into grouped menus in CLO 5.2, including options to revert to previous layouts, and how project file storage now includes multi-view tool layouts. - After installing CLO 5.2, many tools appear missing but are integrated into grouped tool menus. For example, the Edit Pattern tool now contains all point and line editing tools accessible via press-and-hold. - To revert to the old tool layout, navigate to **User Settings > User Interface**, and disable the **Tool Group** option. - Project files now save both the project data and tool layout. Previously, only single-view layouts were saved; now layouts with four views can be saved. - To enable saving four-view layouts, go to **Settings > User Settings > Default File**, and enable the shortcut option for saving four angles. --- ## Sticker Classification and Quick Photo/Video Functions Explains enhancements to sticker classification for logos and custom types, and improvements to quick photo and video capture including HTML outputs. - Stickers can now be classified via the **Attribute Editor** under the Classification box. - Three preset classifications exist; users can create custom ones (e.g., “Four-Wings Print”). - Quick Photo 3D window enhancements: - Save single or multiple quick photos. - Set custom views and picture sizes. - Display up to 10 photos. - Option to save photos as HTML files enabling navigation between photos via browser. - Video feature update: - Added “Save HTML File” option that creates fixed rotation pictures for GIFs or web-based rotation videos. - After recording, both AVI and HTML files can be saved. - HTML videos allow frame-by-frame navigation. --- ## Material List Mode and BOM Editor Details the new Material List Mode, BOM (Bill of Materials) editor, and currency/unit customization for fabric consumption and pricing. - Material List Mode accessed via the upper right corner of the model window. - BOM editor shows fabric size, material volume, and price. - Material volume depends on the sheet placement in Flower Arrangement mode. - BOM editor can be opened in multiple modes; clicking **Update** after arranging updates material volumes. - Currency units can be switched (e.g., to RMB CNY) via the Settings button. - Colors can be assigned and edited, with costs displayed per color and total. - Units for length measurements can be toggled between inches, centimeters, millimeters, etc. - Cost data integrates into the Closet Process List. --- ## AVT Files and Virtual Model Arrangement Instructions on handling AVT files for virtual models, including transformation and arrangement board adjustments.

markdown_content: # CLO5.2 New Features Overview This document details the new features and updates introduced in CLO version 5.2, focusing on tool layout integration, project file storage, sticker classification, photo and video functions, material management, virtual models, 3D and 2D window enhancements, lighting, and Q&A clarifications.
